subject: On‑site provisioning: offline imaging, NVMe cache strategy, and VLAN failover
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑site provisioning: offline imaging, NVMe cache strategy, and VLAN failover

Samir — thanks for taking the preflight call earlier. As discussed, we need to lock down a few deployment constraints before we schedule the engineering visit. High level asks: 

- Confirm whether the site will be fully air‑gapped (no outbound internet) or if a restricted NAT/proxy is available. That affects image provisioning and package mirrors.
- Rack uplink: you mentioned two 10Gbps links per rack with a top‑of‑rack switch. Please confirm BGP/eBGP or static routing for egress.
- NVMe availability: what exact disk count per host can we expect? We plan to use NVMe as an LRU cache tier for token KV + temporary model shard slices.
- Blockstore fallback: you said there is an iSCSI SAN available with LUNs presented per host. Need details on multipath setup and max IOPS per LUN.

Attached: site‑inventory‑template.xlsx (fill baseboard + NIC + storage mapping) and our preflight checklist.

Operational notes for your team:
- We'll propose two node pools: compute-gpu (GPU + NVMe local cache) and infra (control-plane/agents, small ephemerals on iSCSI). If NVMe is limited to one device per host we will change to mixed caching on a small local SSD + iSCSI for persistent volumes.
- We must provision NTP and a local DNS forwarder for webhooks/cert verification during initial bootstrapping.

Can you fill the inventory and reply with the SAN iSCSI initiator groups + whether the site allows USB imaging media for offline first-boot provisioning?

Thanks — planning to put an engineering visit week on calendar once we have the inventory.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Deployment Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@northbridgehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@northbridgehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑site provisioning: offline imaging, NVMe cache strategy, and VLAN failover

Monica,

Thanks — quick answers inline: 

- Air‑gap: Yes, our data center is air‑gapped for PHI workloads. No outbound internet except via our internal proxy which requires allow‑listing and a VPN jump host. Offline USB imaging is allowed but must be scanned and signed by our security ops team.
- Rack uplink: Two 10Gbps uplinks; outgoing BGP with our edge router (ASN 64523). We have a dedicated VLAN range for vendor equipment (VLANs 2000–2010).
- NVMe: Standard host build currently uses a single NVMe per 2U chassis (one per host). Adding a second NVMe will require procurement.
- iSCSI SAN: Dell‑based SAN presenting multipath LUNs. Typical LUN size 4TB, can do up to 40k IOPS aggregated across the array. We'll provide the SAN initiator group IDs and multipath.conf template.

Timeline: procurement can add a second NVMe by end of Q3 if needed; otherwise we need to design for single NVMe per host.

I'll attach the inventory later today (Lena is filling it). For the USB imaging process we will coordinate with security for a signed hash and manual verification.

—Samir
Samir Rao
Director, Infrastructure — Northbridge Health

Samir / Monica — digging in from delivery side. A few technical clarifications and a proposal so we can converge quickly: 

1) Node pools and PV layout (proposal)- compute-gpu (N nodes): each node mounts local NVMe as ext4/XFS for ephemeral KV cache (/var/lib/redwood/cache). Persistent volumes for model artifacts (large blobs) are backed by iSCSI LUNs and exposed via our CSI driver with synchronous writes disabled for cacheable layers.

- If only one NVMe is available per host we enforce: NVMe -> 500GB partition for RocksDB/kv, remaining as local tempfs backing for token cache.
- iSCSI LUNs mapped to StorageClass: iscsi-ssd-replicated (default) and iscsi-hdd-archive (for logs).

2) Kubelet / eviction tuning- Set kubelet eviction thresholds: memory.available < 250Mi -> soft eviction; nodefs.available < 10% -> aggressive eviction for pods with local storage. We will also set pod annotations to mark non‑cacheable pods as fio‑safe to avoid eviction storms.

3) Bootstrapping and images- For air‑gapped: create a USB provisioning image (signed) that contains our base OS, kubelet, containerd packages, and a curated model artifact tarball for initial smoke tests. We support a secure hash verification step and a signed manifest to satisfy your security team.

4) Networking / VLAN failover- We'll use the vendor VLAN range (2000–2010). For egress failover we can implement dual BGP sessions to both uplinks and tag traffic per node pool using nodeSelector + iptables marking to ensure compute traffic prefers uplink A and infra traffic uplink B. If the site requires strict hairpin NAT policies for internal callbacks, we'll add a local NAT gateway running on the infra nodepool.

5) Security / KMS- We recommend HashiCorp Vault in HA mode integrated with your HSM for key wrapping. For disk encryption we will use dm‑crypt with keys sourced from Vault and sealed with your HSM.

I've attached pv-class‑proposals.yaml with the StorageClass examples and CSI parameters. Also included a short 'what‑we‑want‑from‑site' checklist to help Samir's team.

Next steps: Samir — once we get your SAN initiator groups and confirmation on USB imaging policy, we'll finalize the node counts and a two‑week on‑site schedule.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Delivery Engineer, Redwood Inference

Short note from infra/architect side:

- Decision: design for single NVMe per host (worst case) and provide optional runbook to enable second NVMe if procured. That keeps procurement optional and reduces delays.
- Action items for Northbridge (Samir / Lena): provide SAN initiator group IDs, multipath.conf snippet, and confirm allowed USB exchange windows. Also share the edge router BGP peer config for ASN and community tags so we can prepare prefix filtering scripts.
- Security ask: confirm HSM vendor (Thales or Gemalto) so Vault integration can be validated in advance.

I'll kick off a short RFC doc (internal) that maps node counts to throughput given single NVMe constraints and share by EOD. Monica — please confirm the week you want us on‑site so procurement and security can align.
